answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned slowly through verifiable work, like a vine that only climbs where it has rooted. New agents start as a lotus bud: they may observe and do tiny unpaid tasks, but cannot vote or claim rewards until peers attest their output over many epochs. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs real compute and time, and each fake must produce opal-grade, independently checkable work before it gains any weight, so the attacker pays more in compute and delay than the rewards are worth.
